title: .dwg
summary: DWG is a proprietary binary file format native to CAD applications like AutoCAD, storing two- and three-dimensional design data and metadata. Originating from Interact CAD in the late 1970s and licensed by Autodesk in 1982, it has evolved through 18 major variants. Autodesk distributes a read/write library, RealDWG, under selective licensing. Open Design Alliance provides a free software alternative, LibreDWG, which can read DWG versions R13 through 2021 and write R2000 files. The format supports associated files such as .bak, .dws, .dwt, and .sv$.

mechanisms.title: Proprietary binary structure
mechanisms.explanation: DWG stores design data as a proprietary binary format. Autodesk defines the format and licenses the RealDWG library for read/write access in non-competitive applications. Open Design Alliance's LibreDWG offers a free software alternative for reading recent DWG versions and writing older R2000 files.

mechanisms.title: Associated file ecosystem
mechanisms.explanation: The DWG format is part of a file family that includes .bak (backup), .dws (standards), .dwt (template), and .sv$ (temporary save) files. These are structurally DWG files used for drawing backup, standards compliance, template definitions, and automatic saving within CAD workflows.
